structured_output.summary: This change passes all 23 checklist items. It adds `OrderPage.cancel()` along with two locators: the header menu button, scoped to `page-header` so it doesn't match the order-lines menu, and the cancel menu item. It also adds one spec built on the suite fixture and `ORDERS_SCENARIO`. The spec opens the scenario's unpaid order with `findOrderId`. Before acting, it checks that the order reads Unfulfilled and that the fulfil action is offered. It then cancels the order and confirms that the status reads Cancelled and the fulfil button is gone. After a reload it checks both again, which proves the cancellation was saved on the server. The type check passed with no errors.

items.evidence: After `page.reload()` the status-info still reads "Cancelled" and the fulfil button stays hidden (diff 68-72), so the test fails if the server never cancels the order.
Each criterion is asserted: status Cancelled (diff 64), no fulfil action (diff 65), and Cancelled after reload (diff 69-70).
`OrderPage` has no menu or cancel action yet, so the new members extend the existing page object. The spec reuses `statusInfo`, `fulfillButton`, `dialog`, `findOrderId` and `ORDERS_SCENARIO`.
No fixed waits. `cancel()` waits for the dialog to close, and the spec uses web-first assertions.
`test` comes from `../../fixtures/test.ts`, the test is not tagged `parallel()`, and nothing writes to the cache or the dumps.
Locators use test ids. `show-more-button` is scoped to `page-header` and the submit button to the dialog. `cancel-order` exists only in the order page menu.
The spec uses the scenario's existing unpaid order and creates no data.
The order is looked up with `findOrderId(config, "unpaid")`. No ids or populatedb values are hard-coded.
The spec uses the default admin stored session, and the ticket names no permission actor. It does not sign in through the UI.
The spec is in `e2e/tests/orders/`, and `typecheck.txt` reports "exit 0: no errors".
All locators and the cancel flow live on `OrderPage`. The spec only calls methods and asserts on page-object locators.
The new members are `readonly` fields initialised from `this.page`, and the existing constructor is unchanged.
The spec has `// Arrange` (diff 53) and `// Act & Assert` (diff 61).
It is one test with a `test.step` for each stage: cancel, then the saved check.
The title describes the behaviour and carries `#e2e`.
A header comment (diff 42-45) says what the spec covers and why it matters.
All assertions are web-first: `toHaveText`, `toBeVisible` and `toBeHidden`.
The scenario is the `ORDERS_SCENARIO` constant. The status strings are UI labels with no exported constants, and the test involves no money or arithmetic.
No cleanup code and no unique names.
No custom timeouts, retries, `networkidle` or `waitForLoadState`.
Relative imports keep the `.ts` extension, and nothing is imported from `@playwright/test`.
No `any`, no casts, and no untyped `gql` calls.
The comments explain reasons: why the menu locator is scoped (diff 9) and why fulfil is checked before cancelling (diff 57).
